sources.excerpt: Fade Font ’94 – High-Gain Vintage BM Distortion Recreation — Wren and Cuff Home Pedals All Pedals Muffs Distortion/Fuzz Boost and Compression Info Shipping Warranty Repairs Artists About Us FAQ's Gift Cards Apparel Dealers Contact B-Stock Home Pedals All Pedals Muffs Distortion/Fuzz Boost and Compression Info Shipping Warranty Repairs Artists About Us FAQ's Gift Cards Apparel Dealers Contact B-Stock Pedals All Hidden Newsletter ← Back to Pedals Fade Font '94 Fade Font '94 $324.99 From 1994 to You Heavy duty full-size folded steel enclosure All through-hole components True hard-wire bypass Made in Los Angeles Quantity: Add To Cart The louder, more aggressive sibling of the legacy classic, Tall Font Russian, the Fade Font draws its inspiration from one of Matt’s other most beloved vintage Russian-made muffers from 1994. This particular muff stood apart, featuring 150K pots (rather than the 100K found in almost every other BM version) and unique component values not present in earlier models. Factor in time-drift and a 15% variance in values, and the result was a tone so distinct it demanded careful deconstruction to reproduce. The goal? Recreate the legendary high-gain, papery grit, and commanding, focused low-end that have made this circuit a favorite among guitar and bass players. After nearly two years of meticulous revisions and experimentation—including custom-fabricated 150K pots with precise tapers—the circuit was finally perfected. Why is it called the “Fade Font ‘94”? The name nods to a unique quirk of the original 1994 pedals: their graphics, printed with low-quality powder-coat and ink, often faded dramatically over time. This detail became a defining characteristic of these vintage USSR-made BM pedals, adding another layer of charm to their legacy. To complete the experience, we designed an enclosure that mirrors the dimensions of the original design. This full-sized recreation faithfully replicates the robust, iconic aesthetic while ensuring a durable build that will stand the test of time. It’s a pedal made to honor its heritage while delivering exceptional performance for years to come. Wait, explain more about the difference between this and the Wren and Cuff Tall Font Russian. Is this just a full-size version of that pedal? NO! This is a completely different circuit. The Tall Font Russian is based on Matt’s #1 Sov BM, a transitional version Tall Font from late ’94/’95. That pedal finds its beauty on the opposite end of the spectrum because of its oddball low output, low gain bordering on overdrive, and less extreme tone range. These are intentionally two different tools, each with its own character and merit. Whether you’re chasing vintage authenticity or shaping your unique sound, the Fade Font ’94 delivers a bold, unmistakable voice that stands as a true testament to its legendary inspiration.
